note:
TECHNIQUE -- `census-run.sh status` UNDER-REPORTS A BUSY BOX, AND CLAUDE.md CALLS IT THE AUTHORITATIVE CHECK. Measured 2026-09-10, 25 minutes into campaign/underworld-peoples' queued census.

WHAT I OBSERVED, all four at the same moment, box demonstrably occupied:

    $ fuser -v /tmp/hv-census.lock
    /tmp/hv-census.lock: nathan  1802147 F.... bash      <- sluice-census.sh
                         nathan  1825951 F.... bash
    $ ls /tmp/hv-census.claim
      (does not exist)
    $ bash scripts/census-run.sh status
    no heavy run in progress
    $ ps -o etime= -p 1802147
      25:26

THE MECHANISM, from the source rather than inferred: `status` delegates to
`lab claim-status`, which reads /tmp/hv-census.claim. census-run.sh WRITES
that file at line 213 and `rm -f`s it on EXIT at line 216 -- so the claim
exists exactly for census-run.sh's own lifetime. But a QUEUED census runs
under scripts/sluice-census.sh, which takes the shared flock and holds it
across setup AND the post-measurement commit/push, both OUTSIDE that lifetime.

    the flock  = the whole busy window
    the claim  = a strict SUBSET of it

I did not observe which end of the window this was (setup vs. post-measurement
commit); at 25 minutes against ~23-minute recent censuses, post-measurement is
the likely one, but I am not claiming it.

WHY IT MATTERS. CLAUDE.md says `bash scripts/census-run.sh status` answers "is
a census running right now?" and warns that a pgrep cannot see one. The second
half is true. The first half is true only inside the subset.

MY OWN GUARD HAD THIS BUG AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT. My manual
merge-drain refused when the status output matched "running:". Counterfactual,
run against the live busy box:

    $ bash scripts/census-run.sh status | grep -q "running:" && echo REFUSE || echo PROCEED
    PROCEED

It would have launched a chamber into an occupied box. Nothing corrupts --
flock still serializes, so the chamber would simply block -- but a chamber
blocked on a lock reads like a hang, which is the exact confusing state the
guard exists to prevent.

THE FIX, for anyone writing a busy check: read the signals that cover the
whole window, not the claim.

    1. the queue's own running row:
       sluice-queue.sh list | awk -F'\t' '$5=="running"{...}'
    2. the flock itself:
       fuser /tmp/hv-census.lock

Mine now checks both and refuses correctly:

    REFUSED: the queue has a running job — campaign/underworld-peoples (census)

THE SHAPE IS THE FAMILIAR ONE. Two layers enforcing one invariant -- a shell
flock and a Rust claim file -- each correct in isolation, disagreeing at the
edges, with the cheaper-to-read one documented as authoritative. That is the
same failure The Turnstile shipped, and the reason decision 0079 gives the
canonical-host guard ONE shared file for both layers. Worth someone deciding
whether the claim should span sluice-census.sh's whole hold, or whether
CLAUDE.md should stop calling `status` authoritative. I am not editing
CLAUDE.md from an operator session; flagging it for a campaign that owns it.
